https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Sample-Shadows-120x-zoom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] While Magic Capture took most of the spotlight in Google’s keynote, maybe the most discussed photo upgrade this year is Camera Looks. I did a whole interview with Google’s camera chief about this feature going deep into how the new system was made, and there’s a lot of potential in the execution. Camera Looks is a new photography feature you can think of similar to Fujifilm’s film simulations, which let its cameras emulate different film styles on the JPGs they put out. On the Pixel 11 series, there are four modifications of the standard camera, with Original, Natural, Shadows, and Vanilla giving subtle tweaks to your image. But if you want to get more out there, there are six additional creative looks, called Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie, and Minimal. Each of the looks can be modified to your liking, with adjustable settings like contrast, highlights, shadows, vibrance, tint, warmth, sharpness, and grain. What makes this a really interesting feature to me is that Google is adjusting the amount of computational processing it’s doing at capture, based on the settings you choose; it’s not just applying filters later. For example, the Digi mode will do less frame stacking and the Minimal mode will apply less sharpness and contrast. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-9.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-8.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-6.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-5.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-Black-Tie-Camera-Look.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] I really dig the looks, even right out of the box. They span from basic edits to quite inspired, and if you’re looking for something that gives you the “film simulation look” straight out of camera, these definitely deliver. It was high time Google added some more creative looks to the Pixel, especially considering it doesn’t have nearly as robust a third-party camera ecosystem as the iPhone. I’ve personally made the Minimal mode permanent on my phone for its unsharpened, minimally contrasty look, occasionally switching to Classic, but after testing them all, I think Velvet and Editorial will get a lot of use, since they have the most “film aesthetic” of the bunch. With less processed photos, you can actually see texture in photos, which is normally washed away by noise reduction algorithms. Overall camera quality on the Pixel 11 Pro series is great this year, and practically the only reason to pick up a Pro Pixel over the standard 11, aside from wanting a larger phone, in the case of the XL. The primary sensor is technically new, but Google tells me it’s the same size as last year and was swapped in because it uses slightly less power. The biggest camera hardware change is the new larger telephoto sensor, which Google says captures more light, and I can tell. Telephoto cameras are usually the weakest link in a smartphone’s camera arsenal, but even at 10x zoom, which is a 2x crop of the telephoto sensor, it was hard to notice any significant quality degradation. Plus, the transition between sensors is much smoother now, with only a very slight jump when switching between lenses. [Image: The Camera Looks interface. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Taking-Photo-Camera-Looks-Velvet.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The Pixel 11 Pro also includes a 120x Pro Zoom mode, enabled by the new image signal processor in Tensor G6. Like the 100x Pro Zoom on the Pixel 10 Pro, Google is using generative AI to upscale your highly zoomed-in images to make them look more realistic. On objects without a lot of sharp edges this actually does a pretty good job, and Google will give you both the non-AI-enhanced and enhanced versions so you can see the difference. I was in Spain during last week’s solar eclipse, and the Pixel 11 Pro did a good job of turning a zoomed-in photo of the moon from a blurry mess into something that looked good enough to elicit responses of awe when I posted it in Slack. But that was a relatively simple image, and shots with a lot more detail often look like an early AI-generated image, with skewed angles and edges, garbled text, and muddy tones. I’d only really use this if you needed to see information you can’t see with your normal eyes, not for artistic purposes. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-Super-Res-Zoom-100x.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-Super-Res-Zoom-120x.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The Pixel 11 Pro also gets a new, faster Night Sight, which Google says is about three times faster on average than the Pixel 10 Pro. In testing, most Night Sight images I took only needed to be held for one second, and I got all the same benefits you got from holding the phone for three or more seconds previously. This is the kind of quality-of-life update I love to see, and I’m glad Google is continuing to improve here. I love Rambler, Magic Capture, and Camera Looks. If you’re looking to upgrade your phone this year, they’re legitimately great features. But after a week of use, it’s clear to me that the Pixel 11 Pro is not yet smart enough to help me use my phone less, despite what Google claims. Proactive Assistance is only bound to save you a few seconds and a few taps compared to just opening the apps and doing the steps yourself. If you were hoping for the Pixel 11 Pro would help address your phone addiction, that’s probably not going to happen. But if you’re looking for a phone with the best voice-to-text on the market, great cameras with good built-in style, and solid hardware, the Pixel 11 Pro delivers.  Photography by David Imel / The Verge

articles.title: Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 and DualSense Controller Up for Preorder in the UK
articles.summary: Marvel's Wolverine for PS5 is getting limited-edition PS5 consoles, covers, and controllers. All of which are now up for preorder in the UK.
articles.body:
Marvel’s Wolverine comes out on September 15, and to celebrate, PlayStation and Sony are also releasing a bunch of new, rather cool-looking, Wolverine-themed accessories and PS5 hardware.

That includes a limited-edition DualSense Wireless Controller, all decked out in black and either classic "Battle Yellow" or "Adamantium" silver, alongside a limited-edition PS5 Digital Edition bundle and some console covers.

These are all now live to preorder, and you can find everything at either PS Direct or Smyths Toys UK right now. I'll leave a link to everything up for grabs just below. For those in the US, check out our dedicated preorder guide here on IGN instead .

DualSense Wireless Controller – Marvel’s Wolverine Battle Yellow Limited Edition

DualSense Wireless Controller – Marvel’s Wolverine Adamantium Limited Edition

PlayStation 5 Digital Edition – Marvel’s Wolverine Battle Yellow Limited Edition Bundle

PlayStation 5 Console Covers – Battle Yellow Limited Edition

As I mentioned, these are all coming out on the same day as Wolverine on the PS5. Preorders are live, but some of the limited edition gear is already starting to sell out.

Both the covers for the PlayStation 5 Pro are now out of stock at PlayStation Direct, and the standard DualSense Wolverine controller in yellow is also now unavailable at PS Direct and is only available at Smyths Toys in the UK.

Smyths is also the retailer exclusive for the "Adamantium" version of the controller in Ireland, and is selling for €84.99.

Smyths also offer free click and collect on these, but you will have to pay for delivery.

There's currently no sign on stock at Argos, Amazon, or Currys in the UK either. PS Direct delivery, however, is free, which is something at least.

And of course if you want to play the game at launch, you can preorder it, too. Check out our Marvel’s Wolverine preorder guide for full details on what comes in each edition. It's currently down to £62.99 at Smyths in the UK (down from its RRP of £69.99).

Robert Anderson is IGN's Senior Commerce Editor and resident deals expert on games, collectibles, trading card games, and more. You can follow him @robertliam21 on Bluesky .

articles.title: Best Buy Is Offering a Free $10 Gift Card With These Game Preorders
articles.summary: Best Buy is the only retailer offering a free $10 gift card as a preorder bonus on some of the biggest games coming this Fall.
articles.body:
I’ve been covering deals long enough to remember the good old days when Amazon and Best Buy offered preorder discounts on every video game they sold. Those days are over, but Best Buy is bringing back the spirit of the deal. Right now, when you preorder select games (including The Blood of Dawnwalker), you’ll get a free $10 Best Buy digital gift card at launch. That’s the best (and only) deal going on most of these games. Let’s take a look at the current offerings.

Free $10 Gift Card When You Preorder These Games

The Blood of Dawnwalker (PS5, XSX) + $10 Gift Card

Ace Combat: Wings of Theve (PS5, XSX) + $10 Gift Card

EA Sports FC 27 (PS5, XSX, Switch 2) + $10 Gift Card

EA Sports NHL 27 (PS5, XSX) + $10 Gift Card

So what games are we talking about, specifically? Four games currently qualify for the deal: The Blood of Dawnwalker, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, FC 27, and NHL 27. With the price of games going up to as high as $80 this console generation ( thanks, Nintendo ), I’ll take any preorder discount I can get on games I know I’m going to buy at launch.

The Blood of Dawnwalker comes out September 3. It’s an open-world action-RPG from some of the creative minds behind The Witcher 3 – which is about the most compelling thing you could tell me about any game. It’s set in 14th-century Europe, when powerful vampires have taken over a city in the Carpathian Mountains. You play as a Dawnwalker, a human by day and vampire by night, who fights to take back control of the region. Check out our hands-on preview for a whole lot more info.

Those who enjoy performing aerial combat maneuvers can hop in a digital jet on either September 29 or October 2, depending on which edition you choose. Either way, you’ll go on military missions to take part in dogfights, drop bombs, deploy missiles, and all that good stuff. See our preview for more.

EA might not have the FIFA license anymore, but that hasn’t stopped them from releasing an annual soccer - er, football — game. This year’s edition promises “ultrarealistic” soccer action as well as a new Clubs experience called The Grounds, which lets you “meet, play, and recruit new Club members while competing across a variety of football activities.” Note that The Grounds is not available on last-gen platforms. And click over to our preview to learn more of what to expect.

Fans of ice skating and blasting pucks across the rink can pick up NHL 27 to get a free $10 gift card. Out on 9/11, this year’s edition features all 32 NHL arenas, along with better crowd graphics and real-world goal songs. Anyone who preorders also gets a player pack, 500 NHL Points, and WOC 2XP Boost.

Bonus Deal - Free CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Steelbook with Preorder

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (PS5, XSX) + Steelbook Case

Best Buy has one other exclusive preorder deal that’s live now, but it’s not a gift card. If you preorder Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 ( see it at Best Buy ), you get a free steelbook case. Better than nothing! It’s out October 23.

For more info about upcoming games, check out our frequently updated list of video game release dates .

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Marvel Addresses the Greatest Flaw of Civil War 20 Years Later
articles.summary: In both movie and comic book forms, the greatest flaw of Civil War is that the conflict eventually ended. But thanks to a pivotal new series, that problem is finally being addressed 20 years later.
articles.body:
When it comes to modern comic book crossovers, few stories can rival Marvel's Civil War when it comes to impact and influence. There was rarely a more exciting time to be reading Marvel's comic book line than the summer and fall of 2006, as iconic heroes like Iron Man and Captain America battled it out on the page and Spider-Man made international headlines. You can take issue with Civil War's execution and the way it characterized certain key players, but the fun factor and the core appeal of the series' premise are undeniable. It's no wonder Marvel Studios adapted the series to great success with 2016's Captain America: Civil War movie.

There's just one problem with Civil War in both its original and MCU forms - its influence on the larger Marvel Universe eventually faded. The ideological conflict over superhuman registration faded without ever being truly resolved. But thanks to Avengers: Armageddon , Marvel is finally addressing that flaw 20 years later. Civil War is a story that arguably never should have ended, and now, it seems it never did.

Read on to learn more about how this new crossover has successfully revived the Civil War conflict two decades later, but beware of spoilers for Avengers: Armageddon #3 ahead!

Marvel Comics: Avengers - Armageddon Panel Image Gallery

Civil War certainly boasts a strong elevator pitch, if nothing else. The series explores what happens when the general public grows fed up with teams like the Avengers operating without governmental oversight. In the wake of a massive tragedy in Stamford, CT, a remorseful Iron Man leads the charge for the Superhuman Registration Act. Opposing him is his old buddy Captain America, who believes heroes need to be free to act without worrying about jurisdiction or jumping through procedural hoops. Personal freedom on one side, and security and accountability on the other. It was basically the perfect conflict for a post-9/11 Marvel Universe.

That ideological divide split the superhero community right down the middle, with some heroes flocking to Iron Man's pro-registration banner and others throwing their lot in with Cap's underground resistance. And perhaps the greatest success of Civil War is that it actually allowed one side (Team Iron Man) to triumph over the other. The Superhuman Registration Act became the law of the land in the Marvel Universe.

And, as MCU fans well remember, a similar conflict played out in Phase 3. Team Iron Man won the debate in Captain America: Civil War, leading to a new status quo where Cap and his allies became fugitives from the law.

But again, the issue with both versions of the story is that the effects of Civil War eventually faded. On the comics side, Marvel explored the long-term fallout of Civil War in subsequent crossovers like 2007’s World War Hulk and 2008’s Secret Invasion, with Iron Man eventually becoming disgraced and replaced in his role as S.H.I.E.L.D. director by Norman Osborn. In the end, Osborn himself was exposed and overthrown, leading to the general public accepting the return of a more traditional, registration-free Avengers team. After several years of turmoil, the Marvel Universe basically reverted to square one.

Similarly, the MCU no longer really feels the effects of Captain America: Civil War. The Sokovia Accords have been phased out, and the general public generally seems willing to accept the idea of heroes operating outside the law (see 2026’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day, where Tom Holland’s Spidey has become New York’s favorite darling despite being a one-man surveillance state). We’ve seen echoes of Civil War through plot points like Mayor Fisk’s anti-vigilante task force in Daredevil: Born Again, but that’s about it.

Frankly, it’s never made sense that the average Joe in either version of the Marvel Universe would simply forget about the idea of superhuman registration and move on. Is it really so unreasonable for ordinary civilians to expect a certain degree of transparency and accountability from these all-powerful super-beings? Does the fact that the Avengers saved the universe from Thanos in 2019’s Avengers: Endgame give them a permanent free pass? It’s never sat right that Marvel would just abandon the concept of superhero registration on either the comics or film side, rather than making registration a permanent part of the conversation going forward.

Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

Avengers: Armageddon - The New Civil War

Enter Avengers: Armageddon. This crossover has come on the scene 20 years after the original Civil War’s debut, and 10 years after the original sequel, Civil War II ( the less said about that book, the better ). Marvel isn’t actually calling this book Civil War III, but after reading issue #3, they might as well have used the name. This book is very much a spiritual sequel to the original Civil War, and I’m all for it.

In Armageddon, the Avengers again find themselves pulled between their responsibility to uphold the law and their duty as heroes. The series opens with Red Hulk and his gamma-powered soldiers invading the war-torn nation of Latveria and declaring it “New America.” The Avengers and Fantastic Four, along with Spider-Man, Wolverine, and former Captain America-turned-godlike hero David Colton, opt to respond to Red Hulk’s attack despite being expressly forbidden by the US government. That decision has caused a chaotic chain reaction of events that threatens to destabilize world peace and turn the public against the Avengers once more.

Colton himself is the architect behind much of that chaos, as he sets about unilaterally destroying the world’s nuclear stockpiles, Superman IV-style. Colton feels nothing but contempt for the Avengers, arguing that people with great power have the responsibility to use that power to make the world a better place. Meanwhile, a new wave of anti-Avengers resentment is brewing, with even Spider-Man questioning whether the world would be better off if superheroes faced more oversight. The series is putting a fresh spin on the same themes that were explored in the original Civil War, thereby proving that the argument over superhuman registration never fully went away.

As the series reaches its climax in issues #4 and 5, we’re going to see a real doomsday scenario play out. Already, Colton has sparked possible nuclear war by failing to eliminate every warhead in existence. Now Red Hulk has thrown his lot in with Russia’s Winter Guard, while the recently reconstituted S.H.I.E.L.D. has taken a stand against the Avengers and rebranded itself “Strategic Human Intelligence, Enforcement, and Logistic Defense.” There’s a world war brewing, and the Avengers are partly to blame.

It’s exciting to see a series finally pick up Civil War’s baton and carry it forward again. At long last, the concept of superhero accountability is at the forefront of the Marvel U. once more. Not in exactly the same way that Civil War presented it, but in a way that builds on that conflict and proves that the original story’s themes and ideas still very much resonate 20 years down the road.

And we already know the effects of this conflict aren’t limited to Avengers: Armageddon itself. This series directly sets the stage for Chip Zdarsky and Marco Checchetto’s relaunched Avengers comic, which sees a drastically different version of Earth’s Mightiest Heroes try to make a stand in a world that hates and fears them like never before.

Zdarsky teases that Spider-Man and his fellow Avengers will be very much dealing with the aftereffects of Armageddon and the question of responsibility in the new series, telling IGN, “Spidey is the poster boy for power and responsibility, so going into Avengers, he and every other hero are considering what that means."

I’m looking forward to a new status quo for Marvel’s comic book universe very much like the post-Civil War lineup in 2007, where heroes everywhere are forced to choose whether they can operate within the confines of the law. Everything we’ve seen of the upcoming Avengers comic suggests that this team will be underground fugitives, similar to how the New Avengers operated in opposition to Iron Man’s Mighty Avengers. That was easily one of the most creatively fruitful periods for the franchise of the past several decades. Why not draw inspiration from the post-Civil War Avengers line? There’s still so much material to mine there.

And, sooner or later, we can only hope that the MCU looks to stories like Avengers: Armageddon for inspiration. Just like the comics, it feels like there’s still so much room to explore the central ideas and conflicts that fueled Captain America: Civil War. Particularly with mutants like Sadie Sink’s Jean Grey now popping up, the general MCU public has to be growing more and more wary of the many unlicensed, unsanctioned superhumans running around. Rather than let the Civil War conflict fade into the background, there’s an opportunity to revive it and explore the sometimes tumultuous relationship the world has with its costumed defenders.

Civil War is nothing if not a great idea for a Marvel story. But like Pandora’s Box, once you open that lid, there’s no putting things back in order. Thankfully, Marvel seems to be belatedly realizing that fact in Avengers: Armageddon. The age-old battle between freedom and security rages on.

paragraphs: When it comes to modern comic book crossovers, few stories can rival Marvel's Civil War when it comes to impact and influence. There was rarely a more exciting time to be reading Marvel's comic book line than the summer and fall of 2006, as iconic heroes like Iron Man and Captain America battled it out on the page and Spider-Man made international headlines. You can take issue with Civil War's execution and the way it characterized certain key players, but the fun factor and the core appeal of the series' premise are undeniable. It's no wonder Marvel Studios adapted the series to great success with 2016's Captain America: Civil War movie.

There's just one problem with Civil War in both its original and MCU forms - its influence on the larger Marvel Universe eventually faded. The ideological conflict over superhuman registration faded without ever being truly resolved. But thanks to Avengers: Armageddon , Marvel is finally addressing that flaw 20 years later. Civil War is a story that arguably never should have ended, and now, it seems it never did.
Read on to learn more about how this new crossover has successfully revived the Civil War conflict two decades later, but beware of spoilers for Avengers: Armageddon #3 ahead!
Marvel Comics: Avengers - Armageddon Panel Image Gallery

Civil War certainly boasts a strong elevator pitch, if nothing else. The series explores what happens when the general public grows fed up with teams like the Avengers operating without governmental oversight. In the wake of a massive tragedy in Stamford, CT, a remorseful Iron Man leads the charge for the Superhuman Registration Act. Opposing him is his old buddy Captain America, who believes heroes need to be free to act without worrying about jurisdiction or jumping through procedural hoops. Personal freedom on one side, and security and accountability on the other. It was basically the perfect conflict for a post-9/11 Marvel Universe.

That ideological divide split the superhero community right down the middle, with some heroes flocking to Iron Man's pro-registration banner and others throwing their lot in with Cap's underground resistance. And perhaps the greatest success of Civil War is that it actually allowed one side (Team Iron Man) to triumph over the other. The Superhuman Registration Act became the law of the land in the Marvel Universe.

And, as MCU fans well remember, a similar conflict played out in Phase 3. Team Iron Man won the debate in Captain America: Civil War, leading to a new status quo where Cap and his allies became fugitives from the law.

But again, the issue with both versions of the story is that the effects of Civil War eventually faded. On the comics side, Marvel explored the long-term fallout of Civil War in subsequent crossovers like 2007’s World War Hulk and 2008’s Secret Invasion, with Iron Man eventually becoming disgraced and replaced in his role as S.H.I.E.L.D. director by Norman Osborn. In the end, Osborn himself was exposed and overthrown, leading to the general public accepting the return of a more traditional, registration-free Avengers team. After several years of turmoil, the Marvel Universe basically reverted to square one.

Similarly, the MCU no longer really feels the effects of Captain America: Civil War. The Sokovia Accords have been phased out, and the general public generally seems willing to accept the idea of heroes operating outside the law (see 2026’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day, where Tom Holland’s Spidey has become New York’s favorite darling despite being a one-man surveillance state). We’ve seen echoes of Civil War through plot points like Mayor Fisk’s anti-vigilante task force in Daredevil: Born Again, but that’s about it.

Frankly, it’s never made sense that the average Joe in either version of the Marvel Universe would simply forget about the idea of superhuman registration and move on. Is it really so unreasonable for ordinary civilians to expect a certain degree of transparency and accountability from these all-powerful super-beings? Does the fact that the Avengers saved the universe from Thanos in 2019’s Avengers: Endgame give them a permanent free pass? It’s never sat right that Marvel would just abandon the concept of superhero registration on either the comics or film side, rather than making registration a permanent part of the conversation going forward.
Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show
Avengers: Armageddon - The New Civil War

Enter Avengers: Armageddon. This crossover has come on the scene 20 years after the original Civil War’s debut, and 10 years after the original sequel, Civil War II ( the less said about that book, the better ). Marvel isn’t actually calling this book Civil War III, but after reading issue #3, they might as well have used the name. This book is very much a spiritual sequel to the original Civil War, and I’m all for it.

In Armageddon, the Avengers again find themselves pulled between their responsibility to uphold the law and their duty as heroes. The series opens with Red Hulk and his gamma-powered soldiers invading the war-torn nation of Latveria and declaring it “New America.” The Avengers and Fantastic Four, along with Spider-Man, Wolverine, and former Captain America-turned-godlike hero David Colton, opt to respond to Red Hulk’s attack despite being expressly forbidden by the US government. That decision has caused a chaotic chain reaction of events that threatens to destabilize world peace and turn the public against the Avengers once more.

Colton himself is the architect behind much of that chaos, as he sets about unilaterally destroying the world’s nuclear stockpiles, Superman IV-style. Colton feels nothing but contempt for the Avengers, arguing that people with great power have the responsibility to use that power to make the world a better place. Meanwhile, a new wave of anti-Avengers resentment is brewing, with even Spider-Man questioning whether the world would be better off if superheroes faced more oversight. The series is putting a fresh spin on the same themes that were explored in the original Civil War, thereby proving that the argument over superhuman registration never fully went away.

As the series reaches its climax in issues #4 and 5, we’re going to see a real doomsday scenario play out. Already, Colton has sparked possible nuclear war by failing to eliminate every warhead in existence. Now Red Hulk has thrown his lot in with Russia’s Winter Guard, while the recently reconstituted S.H.I.E.L.D. has taken a stand against the Avengers and rebranded itself “Strategic Human Intelligence, Enforcement, and Logistic Defense.” There’s a world war brewing, and the Avengers are partly to blame.

It’s exciting to see a series finally pick up Civil War’s baton and carry it forward again. At long last, the concept of superhero accountability is at the forefront of the Marvel U. once more. Not in exactly the same way that Civil War presented it, but in a way that builds on that conflict and proves that the original story’s themes and ideas still very much resonate 20 years down the road.

And we already know the effects of this conflict aren’t limited to Avengers: Armageddon itself. This series directly sets the stage for Chip Zdarsky and Marco Checchetto’s relaunched Avengers comic, which sees a drastically different version of Earth’s Mightiest Heroes try to make a stand in a world that hates and fears them like never before.

Zdarsky teases that Spider-Man and his fellow Avengers will be very much dealing with the aftereffects of Armageddon and the question of responsibility in the new series, telling IGN, “Spidey is the poster boy for power and responsibility, so going into Avengers, he and every other hero are considering what that means."

I’m looking forward to a new status quo for Marvel’s comic book universe very much like the post-Civil War lineup in 2007, where heroes everywhere are forced to choose whether they can operate within the confines of the law. Everything we’ve seen of the upcoming Avengers comic suggests that this team will be underground fugitives, similar to how the New Avengers operated in opposition to Iron Man’s Mighty Avengers. That was easily one of the most creatively fruitful periods for the franchise of the past several decades. Why not draw inspiration from the post-Civil War Avengers line? There’s still so much material to mine there.

And, sooner or later, we can only hope that the MCU looks to stories like Avengers: Armageddon for inspiration. Just like the comics, it feels like there’s still so much room to explore the central ideas and conflicts that fueled Captain America: Civil War. Particularly with mutants like Sadie Sink’s Jean Grey now popping up, the general MCU public has to be growing more and more wary of the many unlicensed, unsanctioned superhumans running around. Rather than let the Civil War conflict fade into the background, there’s an opportunity to revive it and explore the sometimes tumultuous relationship the world has with its costumed defenders.

Civil War is nothing if not a great idea for a Marvel story. But like Pandora’s Box, once you open that lid, there’s no putting things back in order. Thankfully, Marvel seems to be belatedly realizing that fact in Avengers: Armageddon. The age-old battle between freedom and security rages on.

articles.title: Australia says Roblox hasn’t fixed its child predator problem
articles.summary: Roblox is promising more changes to its child safety features after Australia’s online safety regulator found issues, including that adults could send connection requests to children.
articles.body: Roblox is promising more changes to its child safety features following testing from Australia’s online safety regulator, eSafety. eSafety has been looking into concerns that the company hasn’t been in compliance with Australia’s Online Safety Act, including “allegedly failing to have sufficient measures in place to prevent contact between adults and children under 16.” While Roblox has put some new safety measures in place, eSafety’s testing this year found that the platform “continued to put children at risk, including allowing contact between children and adult strangers.” eSafety’s testing found that: > adults could send connection requests to young Australian children without parental or carer consent;  > children and adults could view and respond to one another’s posts on forums outside game environments without parental or carer consent;  > children’s connections were visible to anyone on the Roblox platform; > children’s profiles and biographies, including account names, number and names of connections, avatar images, and non-sensitive biographical information such as their interests were visible to anyone on the Roblox platform, with no option to restrict the visibility of this information. Roblox believes it meets its Online Safety Act obligations, according to eSafety. But the company will be adding further safety measures that include: > preventing adults from contacting unknown children without parental consent > strengthening the account settings of children’s accounts so they are private by default > accessible reporting mechanisms that notify users of complaint outcomes  > engaging an independent third-party auditor to assess the effectiveness of its safety measures, including the deployment of its age-estimation measures. ”This undertaking follows constructive dialogue with eSafety, Australia’s online safety regulator, and reflects our commitment to working with regulators and policymakers around the world to help keep kids safe online,” Nicky Jackson Colaço, Roblox’s global head of public policy, says in a statement. “Our recent rollout of industry leading safety features on Roblox, including Roblox Kids and Select accounts tailored specifically for users under 16, is one of many examples of this commitment.” In the US, Roblox is under investigation by a Senate subcommittee and has been sued by multiple states over alleged child safety issues, though it has settled some state lawsuits. Update, August 20th: Added Roblox statement.

articles.title: Nitro Deck 2 Is Finally Out for Switch 2 on Friday
articles.summary: It's nearly here: the Nitro Deck 2 controller for Switch 2 is set to release August 28.
articles.body:
I love the Nintendo Switch 2. It’s like the original Switch, but it can actually play modern games made by companies other than Nintendo. But despite releasing eight years after the OG Switch, the Switch 2 has the same big problem as its predecessor: I find the Joy-Cons that come with it uncomfortable to use.

Thankfully, third-party accessory makers are finally swooping in to replace them. One of our favorite original Switch accessories was the Nitro Deck, but it's not compatible with Switch 2. Enter the Nitro Deck 2 from CRKD which, after numerous delays , is finally shipping on Friday, August 28 ( see it at Amazon ), in three color options, with an additional one available exclusively at CRKD . The Nitro Deck 2 is designed to make the Switch 2 feel more comfortable in your hands.

The big new feature in this model versus the original Nitro Deck is that you can use it on the Switch 2 in handheld mode, or you can collapse it into a standard controller and use it to play in docked mode. That makes it twice as useful and minimizes the number of controllers you need to buy.

Unlike Joy-Con 2 sticks, the Nitro Deck 2 has full-sized thumbsticks, like the ones on the Pro Controller. They’re CaptiSticks which, like Hall Effect sticks, won't contract stick drift after using for a while. You can also adjust the resistance on them to your liking, and you can swap the stick tops and D-pad with the designs you like best (sold separately – see the alternates on CRKD ).

It also has four back buttons, two extra shoulder buttons, and fully re-mappable controls to give you more gameplay options than a standard controller. And thanks to a tightening dial on the back of the device, it’s also fully compatible with the original Switch and Switch OLED, which is a fun bonus if you still have one of those lying around.

What makes the default Switch 2 Joy-Cons so bad? Let me count the ways. The thumbsticks are too short for comfort. The grips are too thin, giving your hands little to hold onto. The face buttons are tiny. Playing a game using a single Joy-Con turned on its side feels terrible, but using two Joy-Cons also feel awkward and flat when snapped into a grip. To me, they basically feel awkward to use all the time.

Granted, these issues all arise as a result of Nintendo making the Joy-Cons 2 as versatile as possible. And to Nintendo's credit, they really can be used in a whole bunch of ways, some of which come in handy in certain situations. But when you make a controller a jack of all trades, it becomes a master of none. The ways I use my Switch 2 most – in handheld mode or in docked mode – the Joy-Cons just don't cut it.

If you ask me, the best thing to do with your default Joy-Cons 2 is to chuck them in the garbage and replace them with something else – like a Nitro Deck 2, perhaps?

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.body:

And with all the streaming services deciding they can raise prices whenever they want, and plop an hour's worth of ads into your viewing experience, owning your favorites on physical media keeps on looking better and better. articles.title: Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer Delivers a Blood-Drenched Comic Book Epic
articles.summary: The wildly popular action-horror comic Exquisite Corpses is getting a new spinoff focused on the Fox Mask Killer, and we've got a blood-drenched new preview of all the gory fun.
articles.body:
As far as horror comics go, Exquisite Corpses certainly boasts a novel format. Technically, the series is created by James Tynion IV and Michael Walsh, but in the spirit of the exquisite corpse concept, each issue shifts to a new creative team, who tell a story about one of the stylish killers in this action-horror universe. And sometimes, these new stories are so good they just demand a spinoff. That's where Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer comes in.

IGN can exclusively debut a new preview of Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer #1. Check out the slideshow gallery below to see three brand-new interior pages and the previously revealed cover art, but beware of some violent imagery ahead:

Exquisite Corpses: Fox Killer #1 Preview Gallery

As mentioned, Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer is a spinoff of the main series, reuniting writer Che Grayson (Absolute Catwoman), artist Adam Gorham (Infernal Hulk), and colorist Jordie Bellaire (Wonder Woman) as they delve much deeper into the hyperviolent world of the titular masked assassin. Like Exquisite Corpses, Fox Mask Killer is published through Tynion's Tiny Onion imprint and Image Comics.

Here's Tiny Onion's official summary of the new series:

Among killers-for-hire, there are a select few feared even among other assassins. The enigmatic Fox Mask Killer is at the top of that list. But now she wants the one thing even she can’t have – she wants out. And the only person who can offer her an opportunity to get away from her old life may be the devil herself…Discover the thrilling – and tragic – backstory of Exquisite Corpses’ most emblematic killer.

“From the moment James and Michael welcomed me into the world of Exquisite Corpses, I knew it was something special,” said Grayson in a statement. “I gravitated instantly to Fox Mask Killer, a character whose design alone provoked a rich backstory and undeniable aura. With this new limited series, the mask finally comes off, and I couldn’t be more excited to team up again with my best mate Adam alongside stellar talents Jordie and Becca. This is a dream project for me and I think fans of Fox Mask Killer and the Exquisite Corpses series are going to be very happy with the high stakes and even higher emotions thrill ride we have her on.”

articles.title: Duchess of Sussex Meghan Markle is Reportedly Getting Back Into Acting
articles.summary: Meghan Markle, The Duchess of Sussex, is reportedly eyeing a return to acting.
articles.body:
UPDATE: Deadline has reported that Markle has had preliminary conversations to join Guy Ritchie’s Netflix series The Gentlemen, should it be renewed for a third season.

ORIGINAL STORY: Meghan Markle, The Duchess of Sussex, is reportedly eyeing a return to acting.

After a lengthy break from performing — ever since her 2018 marriage to the U.K.'s Prince Harry — Markle has reportedly now been "offered a role in an upcoming project based in the U.K.," according to News.com.au . No further information about the role or production has been made public.

The timing of this news is interesting, as it comes just days after it was widely reported that both Harry and Meghan would soon move back to the U.K. for an extended period after six years living in California. During that time, Markle made appearances in various documentary and lifestyle series, though refrained from taking on fresh acting roles.

The British Royal Family in Movies and TV

Markle began her career with guest spots in TV series such as Knight Rider, Fringe, 90210, and CSI: Miami, before her breakthough role as Rachel Zane in legal drama Suits, a character she played between 2011 to 2018. It was during this time that she met Prince Harry, and the two subsequently married.

Markle's time as a working member of the Royal Family saw her focus on official duties with Harry rather than her acting roles. But Markle has so far failed to return to her former profession even after the couple's high-profile decision to step back from royal life and live in the U.S.

There has been no suggestion that Harry and Meghan's return to the U.K. will include a return to royal duties, and the couple will live in a private residence. The move follows a rare visit in July to see Harry's father, King Charles III. A BBC News report into this latest development includes mention of a royal source that stated they understood "the King was unaware of the move before last weekend, but he welcomes the opportunity to see more of the Sussex family in a private and personal capacity."

Image credit: Fabrice Coffrini / AFP via Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: A $200 Movie Made by a Chinese Mother and Her Son Just Beat Obsession to Become the World's Most Profitable Film  After Making 20,000 Times Its Budget
articles.summary: Low-budget Chinese animated film Niu Lai has just become the most profitable movie relative to its budget, beating out Obsession’s previous record in a baffling turn of events.
articles.body:
Low-budget Chinese animated film Niu Lai has just become the most profitable movie ever relative to its budget, beating out Obsession’s previous record in a baffling turn of events.

If you haven’t heard of Niu Lai, don’t worry — it’s a roughly-animated CGI movie that released exclusively in Chinese theaters on August 5 with little to no fanfare. Despite barely having any sort of promotional campaign, it soared at the Chinese box office, raking in RMB 29 million ($4.3 million USD) during its theatrical run.

That’s a pretty impressive number, considering the type of film Niu Lai is. It boasts extremely rough graphics and was reportedly created on a budget of just $200 , making its eye-watering profits a massive achievement.

During its first 10 days in theaters, the movie only brought in RMB 7,700 ($1,145 USD), with fewer than 300 tickets sold. It wasn’t long before footage and screenshots from the film started surfacing online, prompting morbidly curious viewers to flock to cinemas to see it for themselves, resulting in a hilarious cultural moment that skyrocketed Niu Lai to national, and now international, fame. Theater employees even made their own promotional posters by hand, as there was simply no marketing budget to advertise it.

So, what is Niu Lai about? The film follows a newborn calf named Niu Lai who learns to overcome his fears in an “abstract” dream sequence. It was created by a mother-son duo, Xin Yumeng and Sun Lifang, who spent five years creating it mostly by themselves.

Earning over $4 million on a project made on a mere $200 budget is nothing to sneeze at, and it means that this unexpected film toppled one of the most highly-lauded flicks of the summer: Obsession, which famously became the most world's profitable movie in history relative to its cost on a budget of less than $1 million .

With almost no marketing budget but plenty of unexpected hype, Niu Lai has cinemas across China making their own promotional posters by hand. Theater staff are putting their finest artistic skills to work. https://t.co/u2rpHlNUDb pic.twitter.com/mbeHJm4T8W — Shanghai Daily (@shanghaidaily) August 18, 2026

With almost no marketing budget but plenty of unexpected hype, Niu Lai has cinemas across China making their own promotional posters by hand. Theater staff are putting their finest artistic skills to work. https://t.co/u2rpHlNUDb pic.twitter.com/mbeHJm4T8W

Niu Lai has since surpassed that record, drawing eyes internationally as it continues to gain traction online. While it’s become a world-famous meme of sorts, it’s unclear if its fame will translate to cinema showings outside of China, though there are certainly no shortage of curious commenters wanting to see it for themselves.

It’s been a big summer at the movies on just about all sides, with The Odyssey recently surpassing Deadpool & Wolverine to become the highest-grossing R-rated film of all time and Spider-Man: Brand New Day swinging past Avengers: Endgame’s record to become the fastest movie to reach $700 million at the domestic box office.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Fan Uncovers Impossible Cyberpunk 2077 Location Hidden in New Edgerunners 2 Trailer
articles.summary: An eagle-eyed fan spotted an extremely specific location from Cyberpunk 2077 in the new trailer for Edgerunners 2, earning praise from the show's official social media accounts as theories abound online.
articles.body:
An eagle-eyed fan spotted an extremely specific location from Cyberpunk 2077 in the new trailer for Edgerunners 2, earning praise from the show's official social media accounts as theories abound online.

Netflix dropped a new trailer and images for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 on Thursday, giving us a closer look at Weak Kingsley, D, Roman Carax, and Talia Yang.

In the trailer’s opening shot, we see Night City’s skyline through a puddle. It’s a tranquil image that gets marred after what appears to be Weak Kingsley’s robotic arm — clearly damaged from some sort of scuffle — falls into it, while Kingsley (played by the iconic Clancy Brown) grunts in pain.

It didn’t take long for dedicated Cyberpunk fans to pinpoint the exact location of this puddle in the game itself, which they tracked down to a puddle right outside the Afterlife, a bar frequented by Johnny Silverhand and owned by legendary fixer Rogue Amendiares.

Their skills would give Rainbolt a run for his money, and even earned kudos from the official Cyberpunk: Edgerunners X account, who replied to their post: “You know Night City like the palm of your hand, choom.”

You know Night City like the palm of your hand, choom. ❤️ — Cyberpunk: Edgerunners (@edgerunners) August 21, 2026

You know Night City like the palm of your hand, choom. ❤️

Still others can’t help but pick apart the data shard that D slots into his neck, which looks distinctly like a relic — an experimental data chip created by Arasaka intended to map out a person’s consciousness and imprint it onto the brain of another living person.

Relics are central to the plot of Cyberpunk 2077 . One of them was used to capture Johnny Silverhand’s mind, which was later imprinted onto the protagonist, V’s, brain, kicking off the rest of the game’s story.

Still others are hypothesizing that this particular relic — if that’s indeed what it is — could contain multiple different consciousnesses, owing to a voiceover said by Roman Carax to D at the end of the trailer: “You’re a weapon? A weapon made out of people?"

Not a cyberdeck, I did this really quickly to prove it, its 100% a relic https://t.co/AfbTdcwOq4 pic.twitter.com/07ORxaBzkr — Blckhandmerku | 🏴 • New Acc (@CurrentsC40979) August 21, 2026

Not a cyberdeck, I did this really quickly to prove it, its 100% a relic https://t.co/AfbTdcwOq4 pic.twitter.com/07ORxaBzkr

Previously, a fan by the name Kalenko on X discovered a slew of in-game locations referenced in the second trailer for the new Edgerunners season, which included shots of the bridge above the Riot club that connects Watson and the City Center, an aerial view of the front entrance of the Afterlife, the Deravaja Dojo in Little China, and Kabuki Market, among several others.

Edgerunners Season 1 also included many areas from the game, a favor that the devs at CD Projekt Red returned in kind by adding David’s apartment as an explorable area.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 releases on Netflix on October 20, 2026. In the meantime, you can check out more animated series the streamer teased on Thursday, which includes a new look at WiT’s One Piece reboot and a new season of Blue Eye Samurai.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Genki’s New High-End PC and Switch 2 Controller Has a Built-in Screen and Onboard OS
articles.summary: Genki's new customizable controller has smashed its Kickstarter goal, packing in tons of high-end features like TMR sticks, adjustable triggers, and advanced haptics, as well as even more advanced tech like a full-blown operating system, complete with digital display, built into the controller itself.
articles.body:
Genki, maker of some of our favorite accessories for the Switch 2 and Switch , has launched a Kickstarter for what might be the most over-engineered controller I’ve ever seen – and for $279, it better be. The Genki Manta packs in the kind of cutting edge features found on the best controllers out there, like TMR sticks, adjustable triggers, and advanced haptics, as well as even more advanced tech like a full-blown operating system, complete with digital display, built into the controller itself.

Now, I’m all for hardware and peripherals that incorporate new tech and push their categories forward, but I’m not quite sure why anyone would need a controller this advanced. It’s undeniably well-designed – I appreciate the screen centered below the thumbsticks, instead of above like on the Turtle Beach Stealth Ultra , and how the tension of the thumbsticks can be dialed in (literally) on the fly by twisting the stick itself. But at some point you have to ask if we’re approaching the point of overkill.

Genki is taking a bit of a kitchen sink approach with the Mantra. “We refused to cut corners,” the Kickstarter reads. “It is, frankly, a spec monster.”

Compatible with PC via USB-C wired or 2.4 GHz wireless (via USB dongle) as well as Switch 1 and 2, mobile, and other devices via Bluetooth, the Manta has a standard Xbox-style layout with offset sticks and all your standard inputs. It has a 2,400 mAh user-replaceable battery, but there’s no mention on the Kickstarter page of an estimated usage time between charges. Blessedly, it can remotely wake a paired Switch 2.

The face buttons are “Analog Pulse Buttons” that track through their entire travel when pressed, not just when they bottom out, allowing users to adjust their actuation point anywhere between a quick rapid-reset for burst inputs and a deeper one that calls for a deliberate press. Similarly, the triggers have three distinct modes: Digital, which offers a short travel and crisp click, Rapid, which is fully analog but with a short, smooth travel, and Analog, which offers a full, smooth travel and proportional control.

Other features include “maglev haptics” (better than traditional rumble, apparently), a nine-axis gyroscope/accelerometer/compass for motion controls, six extra inputs (two buttons tucked up top next to the right and left bumpers, two integrated back buttons, and two removable back paddles), and a D-pad that can swap between a traditional cardinal layout and an eight-point satellite dish design.

And that’s not even mentioning the operating system built into the controller. MantaOS uses the controller’s built-in color display to handle all the configuration settings that would normally be handled by driver software or a companion app – stuff like swapping profiles, setting up macros, adjusting inputs, and customizing RGB lighting – right there on the controller.

But it does more than that too – and this is the part where, in the writing of this story, my thinking started to shift from “this is unnecessarily over-engineered” to “wait, that’s actually awesome.” There’s a small button next to the right thumbstick that pulls up an “On-the-Fly KBM” when pressed, turning the screen into a QWERTY or Compass Quick Type keyboard; or hold the button to turn the whole controller into a gyro-controlled mouse input. This is immensely useful for navigating the Windows desktop and bypassing login screens or game launchers. It’s the same sort of thing that makes the Steam Deck and Steam Machine more user-friendly than a handheld or PC running windows, except the solution is handled controller-side instead of by SteamOS.

MantaOS has some other neat tricks, like a macro action timeline that goes beyond recording a series of inputs and delays to fully tracking analog stick paths, trigger pressure, and more, meaning you can record a full gameplay sequence to repeat, such as a difficult boss runback (I’m looking at you, Bilewater ). The screen also has a variety of customizable dashboards to display stuff like your active profile, polling rate, battery, and connection status.

There’s even a programmable layer, running on a dual-core Raspberry Pi RP2350, that can load external apps onto the controller’s 16 MB of internal storage. The Kickstarter shows a clip of a side-scrolling space shooter playing on the built-in screen, and mentions the possibility of developing a “Genki Forge” for users to develop and share homebrewed apps for MantaOS. I have no doubt that someone will get Doom running on it in no time.

The Genki Manta Kickstarter is live now, and as of this writing has around 1,800 backers and more than $400,000 pledged – four times its $100,000 goal. The controller will eventually be priced at $279, but a Super Early Bird pledge tier drops the price down to $189, which puts it in conversation with other high-end controllers like the DualSense Edge . That’s still nearly double the excellent Steam Controller , which has its own set of unique tricks, but at $100 also lacks a great deal of the advanced tech found here.

Genki hopes to start shipping the Manta to backers this coming January, but conservatively estimates the delivery window to January through April 2027. We’ll be testing the Mantra as soon as we can go hands-on, so be sure to look out for our review as we get closer to that launch date.

Bo Moore is IGN's Senior Manager of Tech. You can find him online @usebomswisely.

It’s the same sort of thing that makes the Steam Deck and Steam Machine more user-friendly than a handheld or PC running windows, except the solution is handled controller-side instead of by SteamOS.

MantaOS has some other neat tricks, like a macro action timeline that goes beyond recording a series of inputs and delays to fully tracking analog stick paths, trigger pressure, and more, meaning you can record a full gameplay sequence to repeat, such as a difficult boss runback (I’m looking at you, Bilewater ). The screen also has a variety of customizable dashboards to display stuff like your active profile, polling rate, battery, and connection status.

There’s even a programmable layer, running on a dual-core Raspberry Pi RP2350, that can load external apps onto the controller’s 16 MB of internal storage. The Kickstarter shows a clip of a side-scrolling space shooter playing on the built-in screen, and mentions the possibility of developing a “Genki Forge” for users to develop and share homebrewed apps for MantaOS. I have no doubt that someone will get Doom running on it in no time.

The Genki Manta Kickstarter is live now, and as of this writing has around 1,800 backers and more than $400,000 pledged – four times its $100,000 goal. The controller will eventually be priced at $279, but a Super Early Bird pledge tier drops the price down to $189, which puts it in conversation with other high-end controllers like the DualSense Edge . That’s still nearly double the excellent Steam Controller , which has its own set of unique tricks, but at $100 also lacks a great deal of the advanced tech found here.

Genki hopes to start shipping the Manta to backers this coming January, but conservatively estimates the delivery window to January through April 2027. We’ll be testing the Mantra as soon as we can go hands-on, so be sure to look out for our review as we get closer to that launch date.
Bo Moore is IGN's Senior Manager of Tech. You can find him online @usebomswisely.

articles.title: Ultra Graphics Settings Are a Scam: Why High Is Good Enough, if Not Better, for Most Players
articles.summary: Most games don’t actually need to be played at Ultra settings to look good. They don’t even need it to look great. To prove it, I turned down the settings in a bunch of great-looking games to see how much difference it really makes. Not only did I find it hard to spot any obvious visual difference in most of the games I tested, but performance went up dramatically and the smoother framerates were well worth the minimal sacrifice.
articles.body:
I’m a privileged gamer. As a hardware reviewer, over the years I’ve been sent top-tier CPUs and graphics cards , letting me bounce from one flagship to the next. That’s made me lazy at game settings. I often just set the game at whatever the maximum “Ultra” setting is and get on with playing. But by doing so, I’ve just been playing into the marketing hype – and leaving a lot of performance on the table, it turns out.

Most games don’t actually need to be played at Ultra settings to look good. They don’t even need it to look great. The latest upscaling technologies are fantastically good at emulating higher resolutions, and often the difference between Ultra and High settings isn’t something I even really notice if pushed to look.

As an experiment, I turned down the settings in a bunch of great-looking games to see how much difference it really makes. Not only did I find it hard to spot any obvious visual difference in most of the games I tested, but performance went up dramatically and the smoother framerates were well worth the minimal sacrifice.

I’ve been able to ignore graphics settings for so long due to a mix of low-demand game selection and high-end hardware. As I said, my current system is powerful, but I also mostly play older sim games and lighter indies.

With an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D and PowerColor Red Devil RX 7900 XTX, I have one of the fastest gaming CPUs on the market and the fastest graphics card AMD has ever made. It’s not quite an RTX 5080 or RTX 5090, so it’s not really designed with Ultra Path Tracing in mind, but it’s not a million miles away either. It’s more than capable of running almost any game at Ultra settings, at 4K, and sometimes even with ray tracing enabled.

That’s especially true once you throw in FSR upscaling and a little frame generation to smooth things out.

My plan for this test is to run a bunch of games at their very highest settings that are functionally playable – at least 30 FPS – with upscaling at Quality or native, without frame generation, and grab a few example screenshots of it in action. Then do so again at maxed out settings but with Balanced upscaling, and then a final test with everything turned down just one notch. So High, if Ultra is the top option, Medium if High is the best, etc.

Let’s jump in with what is arguably still one of the best looking games ever made, Cyberpunk 2077. If there’s one game that is guaranteed to bring my 7900XTX to its knees, it’s this one.

And yeah, Raytracing Overdrive Settings, 4K resolution, Path Tracing enabled, FSR set to Quality mode, it was a clunky slideshow mess. 20 FPS at best. But of course it looks incredible:

But you know what also looks incredible? Cyberpunk 2077 at those same settings with Balanced Upscaling. I just took these screenshots, and besides a few background details looking a little more lifelike and of-the-environment in the Quality screenshot, it’s very difficult to tell any difference.

Meanwhile, the performance difference meant it was actually playable.

Although Cyberpunk with ray tracing does look stunning, and its path tracing even more so in the right settings, I’d even argue switching it down to a mere Ultra settings without ray tracing looks almost as good.

It’s definitely more stylized than the real-time lighting effects of ray tracing, but CD Projekt Red did a fantastic job making Night City look real and alive, even with baked in lighting. I’d very happily play the whole game like this.

Alan Wake 2 is far from the glitz and ray-traced glamour of Night City, but it’s just as good looking in its own, dark, dirty way. It also eviscerated my system’s performance with everything absolutely turned up the nines. We’re talking 1-3 FPS. Unplayable. But gorgeous:

But it can very easily be both. Switching over to FSR Balanced, where it’s basically cutting the 4K resolution in half, the performance jumped up to perfectly playable for this type of more sedate game play. I genuinely can’t tell the difference, even when running around. It’s really impressive how far upscaling has come over the years.

I’d be tempted to leave it there, but there is additional performance to be had and not much in the way of a visual downgrade from trimming the fat even more. Switching everything to one notch down (High or Medium, depending on what the setting peaks at) and no ray tracing, gets you an almost-as-good-looking Alan Wake 2 experience.

Performance jumped enormously here, and this is where you want to play if you value smoother animation over pristine visuals. Especially since I still had to look close to spot the real differences. During actual game play, though? With a darker game like this where concealment and shadow is the game’s vibe, I don’t think many would notice.

How about a getting-older but a goodie? Hogwarts Legacy isn’t photo-realistic, but it is incredibly immersive. Making sure the game looks good is a huge part of the experience. Fortunately, you can get away with steering clear of ray tracing with this one. If you enable it, the experience is beautiful:

But I’d argue it’s just as beautiful with Balanced upscaling – notching an extra 15% fps for my trouble, and nudging over a more-comfortable 40 FPS.

Switching to more modest settings and dropping the RT entirely looks amazing too. This game doesn’t make enough use of the fancy-lighting technique to be worth it, I’d argue. Despite its prevalence in the graphics menu, this game looks phenomenal on more modest settings. Don’t fear dropping them down a notch or two.

Final Fantasy VII: Rebirth is not as pretty as the other games, but it’s one that uses an outsized quantity of VRAM. Fortunately, the 24GB on the 7900XTX had no trouble with it even pushed to the limit. But then, why would you bother?

Dropping to Balanced and cutting the rendering resolution by 40% didn’t appear to make much of a difference to how the game looked. There isn’t any more obvious aliasing on background elements, even the thinner pipes. Texture details remain.

Dropping everything to Medium/High setting depending does make more of an impact, but even then it’s something I had to actively look for, and when in motion it’s even less apparent.

It’s not nothing, but I don’t think it’s worth it

If your hardware supports it, playing games at their prettiest is lovely. It’s simple, it’s easy, and it looks great. Especially in static screenshots, or in the ideal circumstances. But so do games with heavier-handed upscaling, and even lowering the settings a little doesn’t strip them of their charm, or immersion. That also gives you extra performance and a smoother game, which I think is way more impactful than getting a few extra pixels, or slightly nicer lighting.

The point I’m trying to make with these comparisons isn’t that there’s no benefit to turning all the settings up to their maximum, but that the performance loss really isn’t worth it. Ultimately, it feels like those settings are a way to get better looking screenshots for the marketing campaign, and to give gamers something to aspire to. A dragon that we’ll forever be chasing, until the next game comes along.

Ultimately, if all you can game on is something lower than the maximum – which is almost all of us – then you really aren’t missing out on much.

Don’t look on in envy at the people spending $5,000 on a graphics card in 2026 . They’re getting a very-slightly-better looking gaming experience for the money. As prices continue to be ridiculous , I think lower settings are perfectly fine.

articles.title: The Best PC Gaming Collaboration Collections to Check Out Now
articles.summary: If you're a PC gamer with a passion for cool collabs, you won't want to overlook these killer crossovers.
articles.body:
Customization is king in this day and age, so gaming enthusiasts are always on the lookout for new and exciting ways to show off their favorite games, anime, movies, and more through their gaming gear. That's why it's nice to see so many collaborations, especially within the PC gaming space. With that in mind, we've gathered our picks for our favorite currently available collabs, so we feel confident you can find something that tickles your fancy below.

Secretlab Titan Evo Limited Edition Chairs

Secretlab Titan Evo Star Wars Stormtrooper XL

Secretlab is well-known for its top-tier gaming chairs, such as the Titan Evo , which comfortably ranks among the best gaming chairs of 2026 . With its best-in-class ergonomics and features, the Titan Evo has become a beloved choice for PC gamers looking for a premium seat. Additionally, the Titan Evo comes sporting a bevy of unique collaborations ranging from hit anime like Dragon Ball Z, Jujutsu Kaisen, and One Piece to popular games like Genshin Impact, Pokémon, Cyberpunk 2077, and League of Legends. And that's just grazing the surface; there are dozens of collabs available, so there's bound to be one that catches your eye.

Whether you're looking for the best pre-built gaming PCs or simply trying to find the perfect case for your own build, you want the final result to look snazzy in its environment. If you're looking for some truly spectacular collabs, Starforge's lineup of themed gaming PC cases may be right up your alley. These cases sport gorgeous UV-printed designs for anime like Chainsaw Man, Frieren, and Solo Leveling, all the way to unexpected gaming options like Terraria or Old School Runescape — and they all feature swappable acrylic platelights that help the inside of your build sell the theme, too. Whether you opt for a full pre-built or just the case, you can't go wrong with these stunners

Razer has been a mainstay in the PC gaming peripheral scene for decades, so it makes sense that the company would nail down some killer collabs. And one of its most sought-after includes the Razer Kraken Kitty V2 - Gengar Edition , which combines solid (albeit not entirely remarkable) audio and mic quality with the titular ghost Pokémon's purple aesthetic. It's a positively delightful option for Poké-fans, even if the $140 price tag feels like a bit unreasonable for a wired headset. But Razer went all in with more Gengar items, too, including themed versions of its Cobra mouse and Gigantus V2 XXL mousepad , so you can get a whole spooky set going if you're so inclined.

There's no denying the effect Genshin Impact has had in the world of gacha games, so it's no wonder it's the focal point of so many collaborations. One of the most impressive, however, comes from Logitech G , providing a full collection of peripherals celebrating the game. You can grab a Kamisato Ayaka-inspired G309 Lightspeed mouse , G515 Lightspeed TKL keyboard , and G733 Lightspeed headset . Meanwhile, the G305 Lightspeed mouse comes in special editions featuring character art for Sayu, Thoma, or Shikanoin Heizou.

There are plenty of unique gaming-specific collaborations on the market, but we just can't help but get a kick out of SteelSeries' South Park collection . It's most fitting that the QcK L micro-woven mousepad is designed to look like everyone's favorite stoner towel, Towelie, but there's also an Arctis Nova 5 Pro headset in the same light purple, featuring his silly face on the earcups. If you're more of a fan of the main cast, though, there's a version of the QcK L with funny portraits of Cartman, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny, too.

BlackLyte may not have the same name recognition as Secretlab, but the company has landed some pretty unique collaborations for its Athena Pro gaming chair . Not only does it have a compelling array of game-themed options, including the likes of Wuchang: Fallen Feathers and Rainbow Six Seige, but it's also a great choice for those looking to rep well-established eSports teams, such as Team Spirit, Team Fnatic, Team Liquid, and more. If you're looking for a mid-range gaming chair with some fun aesthetics, you could do a whole lot worse than these vibrant offerings.

If you're a fan of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, it's hard not to be impressed by Ghost's TMNT lineup . The company's Sentinel series chair comes in a sweet Leonardo special edition that has his iconic blue bandana across the head pillow. And while the special editions of the Wraith M3 Pro gaming mouse and Banshee K68 HE keyboard may not land on our best gaming mouse or best gaming keyboard lists , they're certain to get the job done for folks who absolutely love the Turtles. Don't pass up the Oni deskpad, either, which features the full team in their fighting poses with the city skyline behind them. Cowabunga!

Corsair Call of Duty Black Ops 6 Collection

Love it or hate it, Call of Duty remains among the best-selling and most-played games on the market even decades after its first entry took the world by storm. Corsair knows what's up, too, and has provided players with some peripherals branded in the style of Black Ops 6 , one of the series' most well-received entries in recent years. Whether it's the HS80 headset or the rock solid M75 wireless mouse , these BO6 special editions are sure to satisfy Call of Duty enthusiasts looking for a sleek but visually striking set of peripherals.

Billy Givens is a freelancer at IGN with over a decade of experience writing gaming, film, and tech content. His work can also be found on GameSpot, USA Today, Digital Trends, Tom's Guide, and more. You'll find him blabbering on about video games and more on Twitter at @mektige.

articles.title: Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 Controller Is Still Available for Preorder (But It May Sell Out)
articles.summary: The Marvel's Wolverine-themed PS5 controller has been a huge bestseller among the IGN audience, but it may be starting to sell out ahead of release.
articles.body:
The big PS5 exclusive this fall is Marvel’s Wolverine. It’s Insomniac Studios’ follow-up to the excellent (and massively successful) Spider-Man games, and it promises to be a bloody good time . To go along with the game, Sony is releasing a series of limited-edition Marvel’s Wolverine-themed PS5 hardware . Among IGN readers, by far the most popular item has been the Battle Yellow DualSense Wireless Controller. And while preorders have sold out at some retailers, it’s still available at most of them ( see it at Amazon ). It costs $89.99 and is set to release on September 15, the same day as the game.

Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Controller

DualSense Wireless Controller – Marvel’s Wolverine Battle Yellow Limited Edition

Functionally, Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Wireless Controller is a standard PS5 controller. What makes it stand out is the design, which makes it look like Wolverine got mad while playing Fortnite and attacked the thing. It features three jagged claw marks across the face of the controller. The marks are vibrant yellow, set against the black of the grips and touchpad. It looks fierce.

The bottom of the controller is also yellow, as are the shapes on the face buttons and the tiny arrows on the D-pad. On the left and right grips you’ll also find gray scuff marks that add to the battle-damage effect. Overall, it’s one of the coolest PS5 controller designs yet — and there have been a lot .

Marvel’s Wolverine Limited Edition PS5 Console Bundle and Accessories

The controller actually comes in two variations. There’s a “Battle Yellow” one that’s bright and bold. Then there’s an “Adamantium” white one that features the same scuffed-and-clawed design, but with metallic white to accent the black, making it somewhat less flashy. The Adamantium white one was a PlayStation Direct exclusive, and it has, unfortunately, sold out.

Both designs also have matching console covers you can buy separately, though some of those have sold out as well (the Battle Yellow PS5 slim console cover is still in stock at PS Direct ). It’s possible PS Direct will get more in stock before launch, but I wouldn’t hold my breath. If you want any of these items, you’d be wise to make your purchase sooner than later.

For more, check out our Marvel's Wolverine preorder guide to get the rundown on what preorder bonuses you can expect if you lock in a copy of the game early.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

Functionally, Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Wireless Controller is a standard PS5 controller. What makes it stand out is the design, which makes it look like Wolverine got mad while playing Fortnite and attacked the thing. It features three jagged claw marks across the face of the controller. The marks are vibrant yellow, set against the black of the grips and touchpad. It looks fierce.

The bottom of the controller is also yellow, as are the shapes on the face buttons and the tiny arrows on the D-pad. On the left and right grips you’ll also find gray scuff marks that add to the battle-damage effect. Overall, it’s one of the coolest PS5 controller designs yet — and there have been a lot .
Marvel’s Wolverine Limited Edition PS5 Console Bundle and Accessories

The controller actually comes in two variations. There’s a “Battle Yellow” one that’s bright and bold. Then there’s an “Adamantium” white one that features the same scuffed-and-clawed design, but with metallic white to accent the black, making it somewhat less flashy. The Adamantium white one was a PlayStation Direct exclusive, and it has, unfortunately, sold out.

Both designs also have matching console covers you can buy separately, though some of those have sold out as well (the Battle Yellow PS5 slim console cover is still in stock at PS Direct ). It’s possible PS Direct will get more in stock before launch, but I wouldn’t hold my breath. If you want any of these items, you’d be wise to make your purchase sooner than later.
For more, check out our Marvel's Wolverine preorder guide to get the rundown on what preorder bonuses you can expect if you lock in a copy of the game early.
